intro: You're searching for a house extension architect near you because you're planning to add space to your home, whether that's a single-storey rear extension, a side return, or something more ambitious. You want someone local who understands your area, can guide you through the design and planning process, and turn your ideas into buildable plans. We can introduce you to architects who work in your region and who quote you directly for the job.
need_heading: What people planning a house extension usually need
need_lead: Most homeowners looking for an architect near them want a smooth path from first sketch to finished build.
needs: You have a clear idea of the extra space you want, such as a larger kitchen-diner or a new bedroom, but you need help turning it into a practical design that suits your home and budget.
You're unsure whether your project falls under permitted development or needs a full planning application, and you want an architect who knows the local rules and can advise you.
You may need to appoint a structural engineer for beams or openings, and you'd like an architect who can coordinate that side of things for you.
You're thinking about how the extension will affect your neighbours, including party wall agreements, and you want someone who can handle those conversations sensitively.
You want a local architect who can visit your property, understand its quirks and the local street scene, and produce drawings that satisfy building regulations.
context_heading: Understanding the architect title and local search
context: In the UK, "architect" is a protected title. Only people on the Architects Registration Board (ARB) register can call themselves architects, and they must follow the ARB code of conduct and hold professional indemnity insurance. Many practices are also RIBA Chartered Practices. Architectural designers and technologists can do excellent work too, but they are not registered architects, so it's worth knowing which you are hiring.

When you search for an architect near you, you're likely to find a mix of registered architects and other design professionals. Before you appoint anyone, check the ARB register and ask for a written appointment that sets out services, fees and responsibilities. Building regulations approval, planning permission and party wall matters are separate processes that your architect can help you navigate.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the type of extension you're considering, such as a single-storey rear extension, a double-storey side extension, or a wrap-around, and the approximate size you have in mind.
Mention your location and the type of property you own, as local planning rules and the age of your home can affect what's possible.
Explain whether you already have planning permission or permitted development rights confirmed, or if you need help with that process.
Let us know if you have a budget range in mind, even if it's broad, so we can introduce you to an architect who works at that level.
Say whether you need full services from concept through to construction drawings and help choosing a builder, or just the design and planning stages.
Include any specific requirements, such as making the space accessible, improving energy efficiency, or matching the extension to the existing house style.
questions_heading: Questions to ask a house extension architect
questions: Are you a registered architect with the Architects Registration Board, and can you provide your registration number?
Have you designed extensions in my local area before, and are you familiar with the planning authority's approach?
What is your process for handling planning permission and building regulations approval?
Will you coordinate with a structural engineer if needed, and is that included in your fee?
How do you charge for your work, and what does your fee cover?
Can you provide a written appointment that sets out the services, fees and responsibilities?

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for my house extension?
faqs.a: Some extensions are covered by permitted development rights, but there are limits on size, height and placement. Your local planning authority can confirm whether you need a full application, and an architect can advise you on the rules for your area.

faqs.q: What is the difference between an architect and an architectural designer?
faqs.a: Only people on the Architects Registration Board register can call themselves architects. Architectural designers and technologists can also design extensions and may be qualified through other routes, so it's worth checking their credentials and experience.

faqs.q: Will I need a structural engineer for my extension?
faqs.a: Often yes, especially if you're removing walls or creating large openings. A structural engineer ensures the design is safe and meets building regulations, and your architect can usually recommend one or coordinate their work.

faqs.q: How much does a house extension architect cost?
faqs.a: Fees vary widely depending on the scope of work, the complexity of the project and your location. Architects quote on application, so you'll need to discuss your specific project with them to get an accurate figure.
